title: Rate-limit slack repair and ledger reconciliation
creator: Anjali Patel
description:
Background: We observe a class of billing anomalies when upstream rate-limit throttles cause client-side retries or server-side queuing to re-run requests across adjacent windows. These retried requests can consume "tokens" that are logically part of a rate-limit slack allowance, producing ambiguous ownership of tokens and leading to potential double-counting in the consumption ledger.

Goal: Implement a dedicated reconciliation mechanism that recognizes 'rate-limit slack' events, repairs disputed ledger entries, and provides safe idempotent repair actions without impacting live throughput. The system should provide an authoritative mapping from request lineage to billed consumption and a bounded repair window so retroactive fixes do not cascade costs or violate SLA for billing timeliness.
acceptance_criteria: Reconciler service identifies >= 95% of duplicate-billing cases in a 7-day window in staging from simulated retry spikes
Automated repair produces idempotent ledger adjustments (credit or reassign) with an audit trail and signer metadata
Reconciliation runs within 30 minutes for 95th percentile of affected accounts on daily runs
No customer sees a negative balance; any customer-facing credits are reflected in next billing statement and documented
Console shows a reconciliation dashboard with total repaired tokens, affected requests, and root-cause tags
design_decisions: Use a read-model derived from the canonical consumption ledger + request lineage traces rather than trying to rehydrate application state from live services
Represent 'rate-limit slack' as a first-class event type emitted by edge proxies and gateway schedulers with a compact replay token
Repairs are implemented as compensating ledger entries (credit or transfer) rather than mutation of historical consumption rows to preserve auditability
Favor eventual consistency by default; critical customer-level repairs can be fast-tracked via an API that submits a verified claim with operator review
Avoid synchronous billing-side blocking during reconciliation; we will implement safeguards that prevent repaired credits from causing negative balances
implementation_plan: Schema: add 'reconciliation_claims' table (claim_id, source_window, affected_request_keys[], proposed_adjustment, status, operator_note) — append-only
Edge change: emit 'rl:slack' event with fields (origin_stamp, lineage_id, slack_amount, window_start, heuristic_score) at point of token consumption failure
Reconciler: new service 'rl-slack-reconciler' that consumes events, correlates with ledger rows by lineage_id, computes candidate repairs, and writes claims
Idempotency: each claim is keyed by (lineage_id, reconciler_run_id) and guarded by optimistic upserts; repairs are applied via existing ledger-commit pipeline to reuse billing invariants
Operator workflow: small UI for manual review of high-confidence, high-dollar repairs before committing; lower-dollar repairs auto-commit after X hours
Backfill: one-off backfill job to scan last 30 days for suspected duplicates using heuristic (same customer, overlapping window, identical token_count, retry flag) and create draft claims
Testing harness: extend staging traffic generator to create controlled rate-limit thrash patterns and validate reconciler decisions against a golden ledger
rollout_plan: Phase 0 (canary): Deploy reconciler in staging with emission enabled for a single internal org; verify detection rates and false positive rate < 1%
Phase 1: Start low-volume production orgs with auto-claim disabled (audit-only) for 48 hours
Phase 2: Enable auto-claim for <$100/day accounts with operator alerting; monitor for unexpected credits
Phase 3: Full rollout with parameters tuned and documented in runbooks; enable repair UI to support ad-hoc audits
Kill-switch: feature flag to stop reconciler committing claims; audit logs must persist when disabled
testing_plan: Unit tests for claim generation logic and idempotent upsert behavior
Integration test that injects rl:slack events and asserts single compensating ledger entry per duplicate sequence
Load test: reconcile 1M events/day using k8s horizontal scaling and validate latency SLOs
Chaos test: simulate reconciler restarts and verify no double-application of repairs
Acceptance test: staged synthetic workload reproducing field failure modes and verifying repaired totals match golden outputs
monitoring_and_observability: Alert: spike in claims_failed_total > 5% over baseline triggers pager (oncall-billing)
Tracing: propagate lineage_id and reconciler_run_id through tracing and link to PRs/incident IDs
Dashboards: reconciliation KPIs per-customer and per-region; drilldown to request-level timeline
Audit: append-only storage of claim payloads and operator actions retained for 1 year
